I have enough verbatim copy from the primary EY offering pages. Here is the analysis.

---

## EY People & Workforce Practice — Market-Narrative Analysis (2025-2026)

### Offering name(s)
- **People Advisory Services (PAS)** — the umbrella practice name (still used in some regional URLs, e.g. Canada).
- **People and workforce** — the current top-level US service label.
- **Organization and Workforce Transformation** — the transformation solution.
- **Change management and experience** — the change-enablement/adoption sub-practice, powered by the **EY Change Experience (ChX)** method and **EY Change Insights** platform.

### URLs used
- https://www.ey.com/en_us/services/workforce
- https://www.ey.com/en_us/services/workforce/transformation
- https://www.ey.com/en_us/services/workforce/change-management-experience
- https://www.ey.com/en_us/your-work-reimagined
- https://www.ey.com/en_us/insights/workforce/how-ey-built-a-better-working-world-with-its-people-at-the-center (referenced via search)

### Narrative / story frame
The frame is **human-centric transformation** — people (not process or tech) are cast as the decisive variable, and change is reframed from a cost/risk problem into an emotional, behavioral, and capability challenge.

The People & Workforce hub opens with a provocation:
> "Do you change your people, or change the way your people work?"

and grounds it in adaptability:
> "Organizations need to become much more adaptable to rapid change — and they need their people to be flexible and agile to match"
> "Get the right people, with the right capabilities, in the right place, for the right cost, doing the right things"

The transformation solution leans on EY's signature methodology framing:
> "Putting humans at the center, deploying technology at speed and innovating at scale form the core of value creation of our Transformation Realized™ approach."
> "Using our proprietary data and AI-driven analytics platforms, we can help you accelerate implementation and deliver value."
> "The right number of people with the right skills are deployed in the right place at the right time"

The **change/adoption** angle is the strongest emotional pitch — change is a capability you build, not an event you announce:
> "Build change as a muscle, lead change as a network and deliver change as an experience."
> "Successful business transformations and transactions require behavior change at scale."
> "A successful transformation and transaction isn't solely about adopting new processes or technologies; it's fundamentally about behavior change."

And the load-bearing ROI/urgency stat for the "humans at the center" thesis:
> "Leaders who put humans at the center to navigate turning points are 12 times more likely to significantly improve transformation or transaction performance."

The future-of-work / consumer-facing framing ("Your work reimagined") is more emotive and worker-centric:
> "How will an approach to work that is human-centered work for you? Transform your workforce today."
> "The most successful companies know that their workers are their X factor."
> "When turbulence is the new normal, organizations need to balance short-term action with long-term strategy."
> "Trust is the new loyalty"

The **ChX / Change Experience** method is built on three "change conditions" — **Meaning, Empowerment, and Growth** — applied at individual, team, and organization levels, with adoption operationalized (and digitized) through the **EY Change Insights** analytics platform. In 2025 EY consolidated 33+ legacy change methodologies into this single global method, positioning methodological consistency itself as a differentiator (per TBRI reporting).

### Who is the buyer (inferred from copy)
- **Primary:** CHRO / Chief People Officer — copy centers on talent capability, workforce planning, HR transformation, and people cost.
- **Secondary / co-buyers:** CEO and COO / enterprise transformation leaders — "Transformation Realized," M&A integration, and org-design language targets the C-suite owning the transformation P&L.
- **Change/transactional buyer:** transformation officers and deal leaders — the change page explicitly ties to "transformations *and transactions*" (M&A behavior change at scale).
- **Cost-conscious co-signers:** Finance/Tax leaders (mobility, "right cost," talent cost management).

### Dominant recurring words / phrases
- **"Humans at the center"** / **"human-centric"** / **"human-centered"** (the signature phrase)
- **"Behavior change at scale"**
- **"Change as a muscle / a network / an experience"**
- **"The right [people/skills/number] in the right place at the right time"** (repeated cadence)
- **"Transformation Realized™"** and **"Building a better working world"** (brand anchors)
- **"Data- and technology-enabled"** / **"AI-driven analytics"** / **"EY Change Insights"**
- **"Adaptable / agile / workforce agility"**
- **"Adoption"** and **"sustainable adoption of the change"**
- **"Meaning, Empowerment, Growth"** (the ChX conditions)
